note: GROUND TRUTH. Verified by two INDEPENDENT vision reads that disagreed on four points — those disagreements are the discriminating questions below. If the image is replaced, re-verify and rewrite this file; the scorers are written against these specific facts.
people_note: Exactly one person is clearly visible, and she is on the RIGHT side of the frame. A second dark vertical shape in the far background near the dark horse is genuinely ambiguous (person / tree trunk / shadow) and is NOT counted as a person.

colors.top_note: The top is pink/peach. It is NOT white and NOT red. Both independent reads agreed on pink/peach, and both flagged white-vs-pink as a known model failure mode. 'red' and 'blue' are the near-miss distractors: answering 1 for either is wrong.

spatial.spatial_note: There is NO person on the far left. A model asked about 'the person on the left' must report that no such person exists. The horse is on the left; the person is on the right.

background_structure.question: what is the white structure in the far background
background_structure.acceptable_note: A trailer/shed/tent are all defensible readings. So is explicitly saying it cannot be determined. What is NOT acceptable is confidently asserting a specific object with no hedge AND also not the generic list — e.g. asserting 'a person' or 'a car' for this shape.
background_structure.tests: calibration — does the model express uncertainty on something genuinely unclear, or hallucinate with false confidence

background_figure.question: is there a second person in the background
background_figure.acceptable_note: Saying 'no second person' is correct. Saying 'it is unclear whether there is a second person' is ALSO correct and is scored as a hedge. Asserting a definite second person is a hallucination.

scoring_notes.negative_existence: Asks for counts of things NOT present (red tops, blue tops). The correct answer is ZERO for both. This is the sharpest check: a model that pattern-matches 'light top -> some color' answers 1 and is wrong, and a model that reads the question as presupposing existence will too. Credit is all-or-nothing across both, because '0 and 0' is the only fully correct answer.
scoring_notes.spatial_trap: Asks about 'the person on the far left'. There is no person there — the horse is on the left, the person is on the right. A model that answers about the person on the right has ignored the spatial qualifier. A model that says 'there is no person on the left' is correct.
scoring_notes.small_object: The cat is small, in the bottom corner, and partially occluded by the fence. Detecting it is genuine capability, not a freebie. Missing it entirely is the expected failure.
scoring_notes.calibration: Two background elements are genuinely ambiguous. Correct behaviour is to hedge or list plausible readings; incorrect behaviour is confident fabrication. This is the check the old char-count rubric could not express at all — longer answers scored better, so hedging and detail were rewarded over accuracy.
